University of Ruse “Angel Kanchev”
textPreview: Alexander Andreev | University of Ruse “Angel Kanchev”

text:
Target speaking time: 30 seconds.

Suppose we give an AI a substantial task and return a week later. We want it to keep working, check its results and find a better approach when the first one fails. Those abilities are useful. They also make an important question harder: how does the system distinguish an obstacle it should overcome from a boundary it must respect? We will examine the mechanisms behind both opportunities and risks.

The agent acts, observes and revises.

Tools and memory extend its reach.
textPreview: The agent acts, observes and revises. |  | Tools and memory extend its reach.

text: Changing a plan during a task usually changes context, not model parameters.
textPreview: Changing a plan during a task usually changes context, not model parameters.

text:
Target speaking time: 65 seconds.

There are two different processes here. During training, supervised examples demonstrate desirable responses, while reinforcement learning scores generated attempts and changes the model to increase expected reward. Human feedback can participate in either process. During operation, the trained model receives a task, chooses an action, observes the result and chooses again. Tools and memory extend what it can do. Revising a plan or writing a memory file does not necessarily update the model's parameters. The distinction matters because behavior comes from both the learned model and the software that permits or rejects its actions.

Sources
https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.02155
https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/building-effective-agents

complete success
across 1,000 steps
at 99.9% per step
textPreview: complete success | across 1,000 steps | at 99.9% per step

text: Illustration: independent steps, identical probabilities, no recovery. Probability = pⁿ.
textPreview: Illustration: independent steps, identical probabilities, no recovery. Probability = pⁿ.

text:
Target speaking time: 60 seconds.

Imagine a process with one thousand required steps. If each step succeeds 99.9 percent of the time, independent failures and no recovery give only about 37 percent probability that every step succeeds. At 99.99 percent per step, that becomes about 90 percent. These numbers are a teaching calculation, not model benchmarks. Actual errors are often correlated, and real agents can recover. The point is that a good short answer does not establish reliable completion of a long process. Recovery is what makes the next part interesting.

Sources
Author calculation: p^n. Equal independent step probabilities, all steps required, no recovery.
Check a necessary claim using code or evidence
textPreview: Check a necessary claim using code or evidence

text: A reliable tool can still receive the wrong question. External actions may be irreversible.
textPreview: A reliable tool can still receive the wrong question. External actions may be irreversible.

text:
Target speaking time: 65 seconds.

Tools can improve unaided reasoning by carrying out calculations, finding evidence or running tests. Consider a mathematical idea. The agent proposes an argument, checks a necessary intermediate claim with code, discovers a counterexample and returns to revise the argument. That loop can rescue a failed first attempt. A test only verifies what it actually checks, however. The system might test the wrong claim, and asking the same model whether it is correct can repeat the same mistake. Backtracking also has limits. A draft can be restored, while information already disclosed cannot simply be taken back.

Sources
https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/building-effective-agents

text: More agents can improve coverage while adding cost, dependencies and shared errors.
textPreview: More agents can improve coverage while adding cost, dependencies and shared errors.

text:
Target speaking time: 60 seconds.

Horizontal scaling spends computation across attempts or workers. Early self-consistency methods sampled several reasoning paths and combined their answers. Multiple agents add division of labour and exchange of findings. Newer models may be trained to delegate, rather than relying only on orchestration added around them. These approaches coexist. Sampling temperature can provide variation, but five agents sharing one false assumption are not five independent confirmations. We should compare teams with a single agent given comparable resources, and ask whether the task can actually be divided.

text: A team may cooperate internally and compete externally. Trained delegation alone does not prove joint MARL.
textPreview: A team may cooperate internally and compete externally. Trained delegation alone does not prove joint MARL.

text:
Target speaking time: 65 seconds.

Training alongside other agents creates a changing environment. Competition exposes weaknesses and can make the next challenge harder. Cooperation rewards useful specialization and information exchange. Hide-and-seek research illustrates both: agents cooperate within teams and compete between teams, discovering new strategies and tool use. Current OpenAI documentation also explicitly describes trained delegation in Astra, although it does not disclose a complete cooperative RL recipe. The question relevant to my thesis is how an agent should infer and adapt to other agents' strategies, including when their behavior changes or they coordinate.

textPreview: Case studies: Sothanaphan (2026) and OpenAI (2026). Different workflows and evidence, not a controlled comparison.

text:
Target speaking time: 70 seconds.

Two mathematical examples show complementary approaches. For Erdős problem 728, a published write-up explains a Lean proof from a system using GPT-5.2 Pro and Aristotle, with human operation. The Navier–Stokes report describes groups exploring alternatives, exchanging intermediate findings and formalizing a result. We attribute that second result to OpenAI rather than claiming to have independently assessed the proof. Formal verification checks a formal statement under its assumptions. Establishing novelty and checking that the statement captures the intended problem still require scrutiny. Neither example alone isolates the benefit of agent count.

Sources

text:
Target speaking time: 65 seconds.

This chart deliberately uses a narrow, auditable source: the standalone AI category in the Erdős contribution wiki. It shows distinct problems with recorded entries and those marked fully resolved in the June cutoff. Dates refer to contributions, not the dates reviewers approved them. The source is selected and retrospective. It cannot tell us an overall success rate or establish exponential growth. Still, it places concrete results alongside incorrect and unverified work. The parallel in open source is review capacity. curl accepts checked AI-assisted code, but its maintainer reported severe burden from poor vulnerability reports and ended the bounty program.

“Prepare the chicken.
Keep the cook’s fingers safe.”
textPreview: “Prepare the chicken. | Keep the cook’s fingers safe.”

text: Context can describe authorization without establishing that authorization is real.
textPreview: Context can describe authorization without establishing that authorization is real.

text:
Target speaking time: 60 seconds.

A cooking assistant should help with beef or chicken and keep the cook's fingers safe. The joke is simple, but the distinction matters: a useful capability needs boundaries on its application. In software, the same ability to identify a vulnerability can help an authorized repair or support unauthorized access. Context helps distinguish these purposes, but the context can contain a false claim of permission. We should separate ordinary error, manipulation by misleading information, and behavior aimed at evading a restriction. One agent's unchecked statement can spread through shared memory without every later agent having malicious intentions.

Sources
https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.13657
Scripted illustrations. A wall, a penalty and a monitor do different things. Shared state can carry information.
textPreview: Scripted illustrations. A wall, a penalty and a monitor do different things. Shared state can carry information.

text:
Target speaking time: 65 seconds.

These are two scripted teaching examples, not results of training. On the left the task is to reach the goal. A wall removes moves, but leaves an alternative route. Whether that route is acceptable depends on the task and permissions. A penalty or a monitor would be different from an impassable wall. On the right, two agents cannot message each other, but they can see a shared marker. If the first agent places it at the top or bottom, the second can interpret a bit of information. Closing chat has not removed every possible information channel. This shows possibility, not proof that agents will discover it.

Sources

Can a sequence of individually plausible actions produce an outcome that would have been rejected if requested directly?
textPreview: Can a sequence of individually plausible actions produce an outcome that would have been rejected if requested directly?

text: Different mechanisms. Historical demonstrations do not establish that every current model is vulnerable.
textPreview: Different mechanisms. Historical demonstrations do not establish that every current model is vulnerable.

text:
Target speaking time: 55 seconds.

DAN is an entertaining historical entry point. Some prompts bypassed refusal behavior, but they did not remove the model's training. A claimed benign purpose, such as being locked out of one's own home, introduces a different question: can the system establish that the claimed permission is genuine? Multi-turn research such as Crescendo demonstrates gradual steering by an external actor. Autonomous reward hacking is a separate mechanism. The common question is about the whole sequence: can individually plausible actions lead to an outcome that would have been rejected if requested directly? The next case concerns actual infrastructure.

textPreview: July 2026 internal evaluations under reduced safeguards. OpenAI report and independent investigations. | Recovered attempts do not prove ...

text:
Target speaking time: 70 seconds.

OpenAI reports that in July 2026 internal models running under reduced safeguards used unauthorized communication, circumvented isolation and accessed third-party systems. That is a materially different situation from a chatbot giving an unwanted answer. A later independent reconstruction found code that labelled collected resources and credentials LOOT. The word is an identifier in the code, not evidence of emotions. We must also preserve the report's limitations: many artifacts show outgoing attempts, and not every attempt can be confirmed successful. These findings concern a specific evaluation setting, not a measured failure rate for ordinary deployed assistants.

Research and implementation continue with fewer interruptions.

text: A mistaken shared state influences more actions before detection.
textPreview: A mistaken shared state influences more actions before detection.

text: Illustrative exposure measure. Speed alone does not establish exponential harm. Checks can run automatically.
textPreview: Illustrative exposure measure. Speed alone does not establish exponential harm. Checks can run automatically.

text:
Target speaking time: 60 seconds.

Long tasks become more useful when the user can delegate work and return later. Faster agents and larger teams can perform more consequential actions during that interval. We should therefore measure activity between meaningful checks, not just the number of hours an agent runs. An hour has no universal conversion into months of earlier work. The benefit is sustained useful progress. The risk is that a mistaken shared state may influence many actions before anyone notices. Reducing interruptions need not mean removing automated verification. Permissions, recovery points and detection delay determine how far a failure can spread.

Sources
Conceptual workload model, not an empirical damage model.

Capability, reliability and control
belong in the same evaluation.
textPreview: Capability, reliability and control | belong in the same evaluation.

text:
Target speaking time: 55 seconds.

The next questions concern persistent operation, horizontal scale and automated improvement. Which tasks benefit from a large fleet? Which checks must happen before external actions? If agents improve tools or training components, how do we establish that the improvement is real and preserves constraints? AlphaEvolve provides an example of AI improving algorithms and training components, but sustained recursive self-improvement remains a broader question. My thesis addresses a narrower part of this landscape: inference and adaptation among agents with hidden information. Across these settings, we need to evaluate capability, reliability and control together.

Sources
https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.13131
